THE RULE: §15.69.3 r3 - 35 under standard-binary, 34 under standard-decimal, and what it bounds is the SIGNIFICAND, not the argument (cite.py --check 15.69.3 'If standard-decimal arithmetic is in effect, the total number of digits in the significand of argument-1 shall not exceed 34' -> OK, rule 3). The standard-binary sentence is unreachable by kb/Work PB198's documented §4.2.6 decline of the mode (see AR-15.67.3-4). DERIVED BEFORE THE RUN, with the significand/argument distinction as its own probe: '1234567890123456789012345.678901234' has 34 significand digits and is AT the bound; '123456789012345678901234567.8901234E+1' also has 34 SIGNIFICAND digits but 35 digits in the string once the exponent's own digit is counted, so a whole-string cap would answer §15.3's default 0 where r3 requires the value (1234567890123456789012345678.901234); '12345678901234567890123456.789012345E+1' has 35 significand digits and must answer 0. MEASURED: all three as derived.
